book.title: Fables of Abundance: A Cultural History of Advertising in America
book.summary: American advertisements have become perhaps the most pervasive social icons in the modern world. This book traces their rise against a richly varied backdrop. Its range encompasses literature, religion, and the visual arts, as well as economics, public policy, and the history of medicine. Its cast of characters includes a host of remarkable figures in or around advertising, from P. T. Barnum and Theodore Dreiser to John B. Watson and Joseph Cornell. The book explores the ways that advertising collaborated with other cultural institutions to produce what have become the dominant aspirations, anxieties, and even notions of personal identity in the twentieth-century United States.

argument.statement: Advertising in twentieth-century United States became dominant social icons by collaborating with cultural institutions, shaping aspirations, anxieties, and notions of personal identity.

book.rationale: The book primarily explores the history of advertising in the United States, particularly how it intersects with cultural and economic factors.
